title: Exploring the Applications of Generative AI in High School STEM Education
extended_summary:
This paper examines whether generative AI can improve educational outcomes in high school STEM learning, with a particular focus on physics. The study is motivated by concerns that generative AI may either support learning through personalized assistance or undermine it through overreliance, misinformation, and academic dishonesty. It asks how different learning supports compare when students study the same content in a short classroom-based experiment.

The intervention compared four conditions: a control group with no external resources, a search-engine group, a generative AI group using Bing AI, and a generative AI plus literacy-program group that received brief instruction on responsible and effective AI use. The sample came from Tomball Memorial High School in Tomball, Texas, and included AP Physics 1 and on-level physics students. Students completed pre-tests, received teacher-led instruction, studied with their assigned condition for 20 minutes, then completed post-tests and a survey about understanding, engagement, and enjoyment.

Quantitative results showed that generative AI without literacy support performed worse than the control group in both sections, while the generative AI literacy program improved outcomes relative to generative AI alone, especially in AP Physics. Search engine use often performed as well as or better than generative AI alone. Survey results did not show statistically significant differences across groups, suggesting that students did not perceive large benefits from the intervention even when some objective gains were observed. The paper concludes that generative AI can be detrimental if used without guidance, and that AI literacy instruction may help students use it more effectively.
quality_tier_rationale: This is a quasi-experimental classroom study with pre/post measures and comparison groups, but it is not randomized and has small, uneven group sizes plus attrition in the survey sample. The paper also reports limited control over outside-study behavior, so internal validity concerns remain.
impact_tier_rationale: The study reports a statistically significant positive effect only for one subgroup comparison (AP Physics GAI-LP vs GAI), while the overall treatment effects are null or inconsistent. The practical impact appears modest and unclear rather than clearly positive, especially since no significant gains were found versus control in the main comparisons.

interventions.use_case: Student use of Bing AI (GPT-4-based) as a generative AI study aid for high school physics concept review and problem support during a 20-minute out-of-class learning period.
Search-engine-based study support (Google) used as a non-GenAI comparison condition for student physics review.
A generative AI literacy program slideshow/workshop teaching responsible and effective use of generative AI before study.

finding.finding_summary: The study examined pre/post test score gains in high school physics across control, search engine, generative AI (GAI), and GAI + literacy program conditions (total quantitative n=171; AP Physics n≈91, on-level physics n=80). In AP Physics, the overall group effect was significant (ANOVA p=0.011), with GAI outperforming the control only after adding the literacy program; however, in on-level physics there was no significant group effect (p=0.619), and the paper reports no significant difference between control and any treatment in either section overall.
finding.measure: Physics pre-test to post-test score difference on topic assessments (momentum/impulse for AP Physics; electricity/circuits for on-level physics)
finding.std_deviation: AP Physics SDs by group: control 1.355, SE 1.387, GAI-LP 1.225, GAI 1.791; on-level SDs: control 1.700, SE 2.250, GAI 2.199, GAI-LP 1.569

finding.finding_summary: The survey focused on student engagement, enjoyment, understanding, and confidence, but the MANOVA found no statistically significant difference across experimental groups on these self-report outcomes (Pillai's Trace p=0.115; residual df=42). Descriptively, the GAI group reported slightly higher engagement, but the confidence intervals overlapped substantially and the paper concludes the subjective effects were not statistically reliable.
finding.measure: Post-survey ratings of understanding, confidence, engagement, and enjoyment
